name: Juggernaught
summary: During the Second War, ogres forged the Horde's answer to the Alliance fleet: the juggernaught. Its iron hull and heavy guns made it a floating fortress built to batter ships and coastal strongholds.

sections.title: Terror of the Second War
sections.body: During the Second War, the Horde needed ships to cross the Great Sea and meet the Alliance fleet. Orcs had little seafaring tradition, so they turned to ogre ingenuity. The ogre juggernaught became the backbone of the Horde armada. Slower and less nimble than troll destroyers, these great ships bore heavy plating and broadside guns. Their volleys broke Alliance hulls and reduced shore fortifications to rubble.

sections.title: Ironclad Cove
sections.body: Beneath Westfall's hills, caverns in the Deadmines hide Ironclad Cove. Away from prying eyes and royal inspectors, Edwin VanCleef's craftsmen secretly built a fully armed juggernaught there. The cavern opens directly to the sea. From it, the Defias could bypass Stormwind's overland defenses and launch a surprise naval strike at the heart of the kingdom.

faq.answer: A juggernaught is an enormous, heavily armored battleship armed with heavy naval cannons. Ogres helped the Old Horde build these floating fortresses during the Second War to overpower enemy fleets and coastal defenses.

faq.q: Why is there a huge ship inside the Deadmines?
faq.answer: Edwin VanCleef and the Defias Brotherhood built a juggernaught in Ironclad Cove, a secluded cavern inside the Deadmines. The underground shipyard hid their work from prying eyes and royal inspectors.

faq.q: What did Edwin VanCleef intend to do with the ship?
aliases: why did defias build a ship
faq.answer: The entry does not state what Edwin VanCleef intended to do with the ship.
The Old Horde built juggernaughts with ogre ingenuity during the Second War. Orcs had little seafaring tradition, and these warships became the backbone of the Horde fleet.

faq.q: How does the ship get out of the Deadmines cavern?
faq.answer: Ironclad Cove opens directly to the sea, allowing a juggernaught built there to reach open waters.

faq.q: Does the Horde still use juggernaughts?
faq.answer: Orcish battleships were still called juggernaughts during the Third War. They brought heavy firepower to the Horde fleet, though the current deployment of such ships is uncertain.

angles.text: For the Alliance, a juggernaught under construction beneath Westfall threatens Stormwind and King Anduin's court.
For the Horde, juggernaughts recall its naval heritage from the Second War, when ogre ingenuity helped challenge Alliance mastery of the seas.
As a human, you know Stormwind's rebuilders were betrayed and driven to outlawry under VanCleef. They brought their architectural and stonework skills to a warship hidden beneath Westfall's hills.
As a rogue, you see the audacity in Edwin VanCleef's plan to build a capital battleship beneath the noses of SI:7 and the Stormwind guard.
